ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large square, divided by two vertical lines and two horizontal lines into 9 equal small squares in a 3×3 arrangement. It can be seen that the small cells with gray background include the middle cell, the middle-right cell, and the three bottom cells, for a total of 5 small cells. In the figure, there is one gray circle each at the upper-left position and the upper-right position, belonging to additional gray shading; at the lower-right position there is a white circle, covering the gray region, so it must be subtracted from the gray area. The problem gives that the side length of the large square is 30 cm, so the side length of each small square is 30÷3=10 cm. The radii of the three circles are respectively: upper-left gray circle 4 cm, upper-right gray circle 3 cm, lower-right white circle 5 cm. Then reason: The area of the 5 gray small cells is 5×10^2=500 cm². The area added by the two gray circles is π×4^2+π×3^2=16π+9π=25π. The area reduced by the white circle is π×5^2=25π. The two parts of circle area exactly cancel out, so the total gray area is 500+25π−25π=500 cm².
